existing_reused_note: Configurations link to the stored model records by configuration_of; Boltz-1 links to discovery-model-boltz as the FoldBench Boltz-1 configuration does. Two judgements map existing, unmapped FoldBench protocols (antibody-antigen and protein-ligand) with their stored evaluations; no FoldBench record is changed or copied. The five existing judgements (ClusPro BM5 and FoldBench protein-protein) are unchanged and no new source duplicates theirs. No metric block is shared with another batch, and no vocabulary concept was added.

Only AlphaFold3 models are ranked in Table 1; the source does not print the same table for AlphaFold2.3, Boltz-1 or Chai-1.

Table 1 does not state the number of models ranked per target. Its DockQ row (0.544) matches the best-of-200 value given in the text (0.54), so the table is read as selection among all 200 models; this is an inference.
The DockQ, aeTM, aeiTM and aeRankConf rows use the experimental structure, so they are upper bounds, not usable selection rules.
Figure 6 and the text give a per-target ranking-confidence correlation of 0.28, while Table 1 prints 0.214 for RankConf under a Spearman caption; the figure's correlation type is not stated.
No uncertainty is printed.

judgements.endpoint: Median best DockQ among 1 and among 100 samples for AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Boltz-1 and Chai-1 on 106 nanobody-antigen complexes
limitations: Best-of-N DockQ needs the experimental structure to pick the best sample, so it is an upper bound on what a user could select.
Each sampling depth is a separate run with its own seed (seeds 1 to 5 for N = 1, 10, 25, 50 and 100), unlike the single 50-sample runs of the other protocols.
For Chai-1 the smallest depth is 5 samples (5 trunk samples x 1 diffusion sample), so its N = 1 value is the best of 5.
Boltz-1 appears only in this analysis.
Nanobody (VHH)-antigen complexes only; results do not transfer to conventional antibodies or other complex classes.

The set mixes systems inside and outside each tool's training data (AF3 30 of 106 in training, Chai-1 25, Boltz-2 64); the printed values are over all systems, so they are not post-cutoff results, and Boltz-2's are the most exposed.

The curation text calls Boltz-2's cutoff the earliest among the tools, while the methods give Chai-1 about 12 January 2021, AF3 about 30 September 2021 and Boltz-2 about 1 June 2023. The per-tool counts follow the later statement.
Preprint, not peer reviewed. Supplementary tables were not read.
No uncertainty is printed for these values.

grouping_note: Judgements are grouped by complex class through comparison_group: antibody-antigen-interfaces (five strata, from structural accuracy to confidence as evidence of binding) and protein-ligand-poses (one stratum). The stored protein-protein judgements have no comparison_group and were not edited; the integrator may want to add protein-protein-interfaces to them in a later revision.
negatives_note: Only the Smorodina cognate-versus-shuffled protocol has negatives. They are shuffled VHH-antigen pairings that the source assumes do not bind; none was tested. This is recorded on the dataset's label_semantics, the protocol's limitations, a claim and the judgement rationale, and is one reason the judgement is proxy.

summary_proposal.value: Evidence is grouped by complex class, because results for one class do not establish another. Every judgement is proxy: each measures agreement with a deposited structure or how well a confidence score tracks that agreement, not whether an interaction exists, how strong it is, or whether an experiment will work. Protein-protein: FoldBench (benchmark authors' runs) and ClusPro docking on BM5 remain the stored comparisons. Antibody-antigen: on FoldBench antibody-antigen targets AlphaFold 3 reached a success rate of 47.9, against 34.13 for Protenix, 33.54 for Boltz-1, 28.40 for HelixFold 3 and 23.64 for Chai-1. Fromm et al. 2026, independent of the tool developers, generated 200 AlphaFold3 models for each of 110 antibody-antigen complexes released after the training cutoff. The best model had a mean DockQ of 0.544, but picking by any predicted score gave 0.352 to 0.375 (ipTM 0.370, ranking confidence 0.375, ipSAE 0.353, pDockQ2 0.352), and the per-target Spearman correlation of these scores with DockQ was 0.184 to 0.247. Scores recomputed from the true aligned errors reached 0.508 to 0.516, so the limit is the accuracy of the predicted errors. Smorodina et al. 2026, a preprint, tested nanobody-antigen complexes on a set that mixes systems inside and outside each tool's training data. Ranking cognate above shuffled pairings by ipTM gave average precision 0.187 for AlphaFold3, 0.067 for Chai-1 and 0.026 for Boltz-2, against a random baseline of about 0.011; the shuffled pairings are assumed, not shown, not to bind. ipTM correlated with DockQ at 0.736 (AlphaFold3), 0.665 (Boltz-2) and 0.612 (Chai-1) for the best sample, Boltz-2 had 18% confident failures against 2% for AlphaFold3, and changes in ipTM under extra sampling did not track changes in DockQ (r between -0.040 and -0.019). Protein-ligand: FoldBench reports success rates of 64.90 for AlphaFold 3, 55.04 for Boltz-1, 51.82 for HelixFold 3, 51.23 for Chai-1 and 50.70 for Protenix; no independent post-cutoff ligand comparison with printed per-method values was found in this pass.

metric_reuse_note: Mean DockQ of the selected model is recorded as dockq with the selection in metric_qualifier. Fromm's R and <R> use spearman-correlation as the caption states. Smorodina's quadrant shares use proportion with unit percent and direction lower; best-of-N medians use dockq.
